why_relevant: His Triumphus crucis (Latin, 1497) Book IV, chapter VII, is a dedicated refutation of Islam ('Mahumetanorum sectam omni ratione carere'): it attacks the Qur'an as irrational and self-contradictory, Muhammad's character and violence, the lack of miracles, and the spread of Islam by the sword and carnal promises.
fame: Known chiefly as the Florentine Dominican preacher and author of the apologetic Triumphus crucis. The Islam chapter was taken out of the Latin work and reprinted separately in Theodor Bibliander's Basel anthology (1543 and 1550), as stated in Procter's 1901 introduction (read on Project Gutenberg) and shown by the Paderborn digital copy of the 1550 print (read). Later scholarly citations were not verified beyond search snippets.
